context:
Goal: a held card reads clearly on its line and in the box.
Problem (rule): the blind reviewers want each label once and one name per thing; the mockup says both "held" and "Suspense" in one frame.
Based on (read): decision duo-card-in-hand uses both words; the built strings say "1 held" and "Suspense".
Departs from: main uses "held" and "Suspense" loosely — "held" names the state and "Suspense line" names the place, recorded in the repo glossary.
Asked by lane duo-gaps-design-review (PR 237, mockup docs/design/duo-hand-gaps.html). The picks per part live in docs/design/duo-hand-gaps-notes.md.

options.gain: The tint is never the only sign, and when the box sits under the keys the line still says it.
options.how: "held" is the card's state, "Suspense line" is the place. Both stay on screen; the glossary records which is which.
options.label: Keep both words, fix their roles in the glossary
options.lose: Two words on screen for one card.

options.how: One of the two words goes from the screen.
options.label: One word only
options.lose: The line loses its words, or the box loses its name.

title: A held card: keep both words, "held" for the state and "Suspense line" for the place?
why: Each word then has one meaning, and the held line still reads when the keys cover the box.
